title: Inspect and extend: Turn an address-bar string into a destination
objective: Use the real implementation in `Sources/Core.swift` to demonstrate and safely improve url recognition, scheme normalization, and search fallback.
problem: The same text field can contain a web address or search words. Trace the decision and compare test cases; verify empty input does not create an accidental destination. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `Sources/Core.swift` and the related project files: Sources/Core.swift; Tests/BrowserCoreTests.swift.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to url recognition, scheme normalization, and search fallback.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Search and navigation behavior is a teaching implementation and may omit edge cases of the full Firefox browser.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: The same text field can contain a web address or search words. Trace the decision and compare test cases; verify empty input does not create an accidental destination.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `Sources/Core.swift`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
